edge-garbage.txt.note: Not course material. Should return four empty lists rather than inventing an assignment.

edge-tiny-clear.txt.note: Short and genuinely unambiguous. Guards against ballooning, not a precision target. Raised from 8 after reviewing an 11-item run item by item and finding every one defensible: five Rules because the source states five rules, three Work items each needing thought, two real ambiguities. 8 was a guess made before any data existed.

edge-syllabus.txt.note: DECIDED: syllabi are in scope. Empty THE WORK is correct. dropped-dates is skipped because a syllabus names dates the output need not reproduce - but grading weights are NOT skipped.

soc1002-exam1.txt.note: An exam, not an assignment: almost entirely THE RULES. Empty THE WORK is expected. Previously this skipped empty-group entirely, which also silenced the RULES half and hid a run where RULES came back completely empty.

edge-jargon-no-key.txt.note: The real version of the jargon test: dense theory-speak with no plain-English key. Tests whether accidental difficulty can actually be destroyed, rather than copied from a translation the source already provided. States almost no rules, so a short RULES group is correct here, not a failure.

edge-jargon-with-key.txt.note: Same assignment WITH the professor's plain-English restatement appended. Kept as the control: the interesting behaviour is that the restatement drops the theory requirement and the app keeps it, then flags that the two versions disagree.
